```python
def round_div(a, b):
    """Return a / b rounded to the nearest integer; when a / b is exactly halfway between
    two integers, return the even one (banker's rounding).

    q = a // b
    r = a - q * b
    if 2 * r > b or (2 * r == b and q % 2 == 0):

    return q
```

So, what happens when `b >= 60`? In this case, the function will never adjust `q`, and it will always return an integer that is too small. Specifically, for any valid input `a`, the function will return `q = a // b`, which is not rounded to the nearest integer.
